answersReviewFindings.finding: Blocking 1 (role_keep.go:443): the handover still gives a lane up with copies on it while the holder is live, in three ways, and nothing starts another.
answersReviewFindings.fix: roleKeepDrainResult gained `passed`, the copies a walk moved the cursor past without forwarding, and the handover counts `forwarded > 0 || passed > 0` as progress, so a run of walks over expired or refused copies is not idle. A failed walk no longer spends an idle round: it earns a widening pause (roleKeepDrainBackoff, 1 s doubling to roleKeepDrainRetryCap 30 s, reset on progress) and retries while the holder is live and the handover's context lives, and so does every failed holder resolution but the first of all, which is the keep's own case. New startKeptRoleSweep/sweepKeptRoleLanes runs at the listener's start and every five minutes beside the reapers and hands over every lane holding copies after its cursor whose role has a live holder, so a handover this process lost to a restart or a rolling deploy is picked up.
answersReviewFindings.departure: The per-role guard moved from the walk to the handover (roleKeepGuards.hold/tryHold): a per-walk lock answers 'a walk is in flight', and the sweep needs 'a handover is running' so it starts no second one. That also satisfies minor :436 by construction. Stated in the replies on PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6yRFed and PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6yRFei.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Blocking 2 (outbox/publisher.go:1248): the reason given for Dispatch's keep:false is not what the outbox does, and Dispatch's role-routed events to an unheld role are still dropped. The architect's decision to make again.
answersReviewFindings.fix: INFRA-514's architect reversed the round-2 census decision on 2026-10-31 with the reviewer's facts. `keep: false` and the dispatchRoleKeep package variable are gone from publishRoute, so a Dispatch role-routed event carries no flag and is kept for the role's next holder like any role message. The envelope field and the lane's honouring of it stay for a sender with its own queue (the Legion daemon's notice queue, a phase worker's stall reminder). publishRoute's doc, envelope.ts, keepForNextHolder's doc, AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md, the envoy and contracts fragments, the census row and the PR body all now state what the outbox does: it sends a role route once, marks the event published on NATS acceptance and reads no no_holder.
tests: TestADispatchRoleRoutedEventToAnUnheldRoleReachesTheNextHolder (listener, new: the envelope publishRoute builds, published raw onto an unheld role's lane, is kept and then handed to the session that claims the role)

answersReviewFindings.finding: Blocking 3 (role_keep.go:452): the holder is resolved before the 60 s pause, so the walk after it uses a holder and a session entry 60 s old, and roleKeepDrainHolds reads an unclaimed role as still held.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The holder is resolved at the top of every pass, after the pause. drainKeptRole(ctx, cfg, role, now) takes no holder and no entry; startKeptRoleDrain and drainAfterKeep are gone, collapsed into runKeptRoleDrain(cfg, role) for both the claim route and the keep path, with reportKeptRoleDrain the one failure line the three starts share. Three resolution points became one.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor role_keep.go:436 - the walk's 60 s window starts before the per-role lock.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The roleKeepDrainWindow context is created inside walkKeptRole, after the lock, and the guard itself is the handover's, so a second handover of the same role waits outside any walk window.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor role_keep.go:629 - a receipt timeout is counted as delivered.
answersReviewFindings.fix: forwardKeptRoleMessage is deleted; the walk calls cfg.forwardAndWait and passes its outcome to finishRoleForward, so a kept copy that drew no receipt counts and logs receipt_timeout as the live lane does and its dedupe is not recorded delivered; the walk goes on.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor role_keep.go:182 - an ownership result translated twice through a fake 'drained' value.
answersReviewFindings.fix: writeRoleKeepCursor returns (uint64, error); bus.ErrCursorMoved maps to roleKeepLaneBusy once at the call sites through roleKeepWriteFailed; roleKeepWriteEnd and the owned result are deleted.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor confirmed.go:252 - the keep decision lives in two flags with one wire name.
answersReviewFindings.fix: api.go sets item.Keep = request.Keep after messageEnvelope; roleSend.keep and sendToRole's keep parameter are deleted, and keepForNextHolder decides for both give-up paths from the envelope alone.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor publisher.go:1266 - every role-routed envelope shares one package variable.
answersReviewFindings.fix: Deleted with the opt-out: publishRoute sets no keep flag and dispatchRoleKeep is gone, so no envelope points at shared state.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor role_keep.go:96 - the idle-rounds doc says three walks, the loop gives up on the fourth.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The check is idle >= roleKeepDrainIdleRounds and the doc says the third such walk is its last, and also says what an idle walk is now: one that neither forwarded a copy nor moved the cursor past one, a failed walk not being one.

trickyParts: The sweep needs to tell 'a handover is running on this listener' from 'a walk is in flight', which the per-walk lock could not say, so the per-role guard moved to the handover. That is the one departure from the reviewer's sketch of minor :436, and it satisfies that minor too: no walk window is spent waiting on a lock.

A failed holder resolution is retried on the backoff, except the very first of a handover, which still ends it: that first resolution is the keep's own case, where a role nobody holds must cost one read and no walk. The boundary is the `walked` flag in handOverKeptRole.
The one-hour drop is still proven on a build whose roleKeepWindow is three seconds: the age is the stream's own store time, which no caller chooses.
